assignments.description:
For a Coding Odyssey in Discrete Structures, you need to write a code. You should also write a document. 

In the document: Address these issues:

  • (5 points) A sentence or summary of what the question is asking for.
  • (5 points) A list of references and resources to help answer the question.
  • (5 points) A brief description of general assumptions to help solve the problem, as well as key observations from the references, and a discussion of the gap between your references and your question.
  • (5 points) Your code demonstrating your solution
  • (5 points) A justification of your answer that explains why you believe this is the most correct answer.

 

You should put all of this into a document that gives the discussion items above, as well as your code, the output when your code runs, and a brief discussion of your results.

Please remember that in the text there are some examples of problems at the end of every chapter. For example, at the end of the first chapter, in the area called Computations and Explorations, there is a problem that says,

Look for positive integers that are not the sum of the cubes of nine different positive integers.

These are the types of problems that might be interesting for a programming-based exploration.

Bonus points will be awarded for creativity, efficiency, enjoyment, and clean code. Codes presented during class tend to receive more points because more students can immediately see what the code does and why it is useful.

discussion_topics.message:
For a Coding Odyssey in Discrete Structures, you need to write a code. You should also write a document. 

In the document: Address these issues:

  • (5 points) A sentence or summary of what the question is asking for.
  • (5 points) A list of references and resources to help answer the question.
  • (5 points) A brief description of general assumptions to help solve the problem, as well as key observations from the references, and a discussion of the gap between your references and your question.
  • (5 points) Your code demonstrating your solution
  • (5 points) A justification of your answer that explains why you believe this is the most correct answer.

 

You should put all of this into a document that gives the discussion items above, as well as your code, the output when your code runs, and a brief discussion of your results.

Please remember that in the text there are some examples of problems at the end of every chapter. For example, at the end of the first chapter, in the area called Computations and Explorations, there is a problem that says,

Look for positive integers that are not the sum of the cubes of nine different positive integers.

These are the types of problems that might be interesting for a programming-based exploration.

Bonus points will be awarded for creativity, efficiency, enjoyment, and clean code. Codes presented during class tend to receive more points because more students can immediately see what the code does and why it is useful.
